statement: Each workstream below is PASS only where the behaviour it names is exercised by a test that would fail if the behaviour were absent. PARTIAL_AS_PASS and DEFERRED_AS_PASS are not values this document uses, and a workstream naming a fixture as its only evidence is not PASS. Workstreams prefixed CLOSURE- close l9-meta-injector-final-corpus-closure-v1; workstreams prefixed HANDOFF- close l9-meta-injector-topology-handoff-finalization-v1, which this pull request now also carries.

workstreams.notes: The previous revision recorded interpretation of binary formats as not done, on the grounds that the extractors cite line spans and a Word document has none. The premise was right and the conclusion was not: the contract already answered it by requiring evidence bound to a block id and a structured locator instead. Closing it also exposed that the document index stamped one decoder on every row and derived normalized document ids from it, and that the CSV decoder's smallest unit was the row, so a register with a status column was understood only when the identical table was a worksheet. Both are fixed here. See ADR-043. Single-root local-source mode runs no decoder registry, so it has no normalized documents and no block signals; plumbing an unreachable branch through its work-signal projection was drafted and removed rather than shipped as a surface with nothing behind it.

workstreams.notes: The ordering is asserted through a seam rather than a spy: node:fs is an ES module namespace and cannot be spied on, and all four orderings leave the same bytes at the same path, so the alternative was asserting nothing. A defect found by the scale fixture and fixed here: the unsupported_encoding observation was pushed only when a file was freshly hashed. Carrying a prior hash forward probed the encoding, held the result and dropped the finding, so an incremental scan of an untouched disk holding one Word document produced a different Repository Model Packet semantic hash — and through it a different corpus source snapshot id — than a full scan of exactly those bytes.

workstreams.requirement: Read-only probe of l9-constellation-topology PR #18; Topology mutation forbidden; Meta payload readiness and Topology adapter readiness reported separately.
implementation: No change to l9-constellation-topology. The probe cloned the repository read-only, fetched refs/pull/18/head at 5f2b5b553cf73b4d9a2068652dddc0630fd6c540, and ran its own adapter against a real Meta generation.
evidence: Meta_payload_ready = YES. The generation carries document-work-signals.jsonl (113 records, none sampled) and its manifest, each record naming both artifact_id and rmp_artifact_id and citing its own format's structured locator; document-index.json is l9.document-index/v2 and carries format and structured_locator_type per document.

Topology_adapter_ready = NO, for two reasons found by execution rather than by reading. Running `l9-topology adapt-meta-corpus` against the generation returned document_work_signals: 0 and unadaptable_by_format: {"l9.text-decoder": 5}. First, the adapter reads document-index.json's decoder_id as if it were the format and compares it against LINE_BEARING_FORMATS = {text, markdown, csv, html, ipynb}; the producer emits and has always emitted decoder ids of the form l9.text-decoder, so every signal is declined — including the Markdown ones the adapter is designed to accept. Its own fixtures set decoder_id="markdown", which is why its suite passes. The field that lookup needs, `format`, is present in l9.document-index/v2. Second, the adapter never opens document-work-signals.jsonl: it scrapes work predicates out of the per-root Repository Model Packet assertions, so it saw 5 of the 113 signals the corpus stated.
Both are changes inside l9-constellation-topology. Neither was made here, and the Meta side was not shaped to make the probe pass.
workstreams.notes: PR #18 states its own limitation as the absence of per-signal structured locators from the producer, and names emitting them as the change that closes it. That change has now been made on the producer side. The adapter's decoder_id/format confusion is a separate, pre-existing defect on the consumer side, reported rather than worked around.

invariants_held: observed sources are read-only; every corpus test digests content and mode before and after
no archive modified, no source file moved or deleted
no discovered code, test or package manager executed
no notebook cell executed — the notebook decoder reads `source` and never `outputs`
no spreadsheet formula evaluated — formulas are rendered with their last saved value and a note
no Office macro executed — macro parts are noted as present and never read as code
no HTML script executed — script, style and other opaque element contents are dropped, not indexed
no external resource fetched from a document — external relationships and links are recorded as declared references
no secret-candidate content embedded or decoded — refused on the path, before any byte is read
no LLM called; the only network call any code path can make is to an embedding endpoint an operator explicitly configured
embeddings remain candidate analysis: an embedding signal is never a fact and never creates a project candidate alone
no build priority, strategic roadmap or ranking generated
no consolidation executed
the cache is acceleration and not truth: a warm run is required to be byte-identical to a cold one
absolute paths never enter semantic identity or any semantic projection

no fake source locators and no fake line numbers: each format cites its own coordinate, and no block-bound claim cites a line span. The one structured locator carrying line numbers is notebook_cell, where they are lines of that cell

candidate relationships never become source truth: block-bound claims reach readiness, the semantic passes, coverage, the corpus index and the report, and never the Repository Model Packet, whose evidence class is a line span
sampled_human_projection_may_remain_sampled — document-signals.json still lists at most 50 records per format, and still declares the omission

canonical_machine_projection_must_be_complete — document-work-signals.jsonl has no sample ceiling at any corpus size; the four counts (produced, payload, report, manifest) agree per format and per predicate
inferred_root_identity_never_silently_authorizes_history — refused before acquisition, and an override is recorded rather than warned about
RMP_1_1_semantics_unchanged — no Repository Model Packet field, id or hash changed; the export is a separate projection
no_source_mutation — the source checksum before an observation equals the checksum after
Topology_unmodified — l9-constellation-topology was cloned read-only and its PR #18 head was run, not edited

archive_ready_gate.reason: L9_ACCEPTANCE_CORPUS_MANIFEST was not provided to this pull request. Every requirement in the definition of done other than the operator's own private-corpus run is exercised by a test that would fail if the behaviour were absent, and the gated acceptance path was proven to execute against a synthetic corpus. archive_ready_gate.to_reach_operator_archive_qualified: Set L9_ACCEPTANCE_CORPUS_MANIFEST to a JSON file naming the roots to scan, optionally L9_ACCEPTANCE_CORPUS_EVIDENCE to where the counts-only evidence should be written, and run tests/corpus_real_archive_acceptance.test.ts.
